clue.text: Musician's recital stint broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered about, so the letters of recital stint are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A performer's recital slot is being transmitted on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like it describes the recital going out on air, but it is the anagram signal for RECITAL STINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of a woodwind instrument is one particular kind of musician.

clue.text: Understanding group of high-ranking officers

definitions.meaning: a good grasp of a language or subject, as in a fine mastery
a military headquarters or body of senior officers in charge

explanation.surface: Mutual understanding among a team of senior officers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both mastery of a subject and the senior body that controls a military force.

clue.text: What late-night barman will do clearing clubs is unsurpassed

indicators.note: clearing means removing the letter for clubs

parts.note: a British barman calls time to tell drinkers the pub is closing
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A barman closing late at night, clearing out the clubs, is the best ever.
explanation.definitionFit: A record that is the best of any period is unsurpassed.

clue.text: Mercenary perhaps in Irish uniform

parts.note: regular means uniform or even

explanation.surface: A hired soldier, perhaps, wearing Irish uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like clothing but is the adjective meaning even.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier outside a regular army, such as a mercenary, is an example of an irregular.

clue.text: Precious items not given introduction but they have titles

indicators.note: not given introduction means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: pearls are precious gems

explanation.surface: Valuable things are left unintroduced but bear labels.
explanation.definitionFit: British noblemen ranking above viscounts hold titles of nobility.

clue.text: Long walk exciting a priest

indicators.note: exciting means stirring up, so the letters are stirred

explanation.surface: A long hike that thrills a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiring, trudging journey on foot is a long walk.

clue.text: Builders' material is transported round a US city

indicators.note: round means the word for transported goes around the other letters

parts.note: sent means transported or dispatched
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Building supplies are carried around an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: A filler used to seal joints against water is a material builders use.

clue.text: Public relations speech about biography's rapid growth

indicators.note: about means the word for speech goes around the biography word

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
a life is a biography

explanation.surface: A PR speech discusses how fast a biography sold.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapid increase in number, as of weapons, is a rapid growth.

clue.text: Incandescent with rage referring to others?

definitions.meaning: whimsically, next to me, so describing people other than me

explanation.surface: Someone furious and talking about other people.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means frantic with emotion, and literally means alongside one's own self.

clue.text: Rural traveller seeing someone taking risks by river — not good

parts.note: R is the standard map abbreviation for river

indicators.note: not here tells us to leave out the letter for good from the risk-taker

parts.note: a gambler takes risks with money

explanation.surface: A country walker meets a reckless person beside a river and judges them bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiker who strolls through the countryside for pleasure is a rural traveller on foot.

clue.text: Booze, old style, and stagger — trouble by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase says the words for stagger and trouble are to be heard, not written

parts.note: to reel is to stagger, and to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned drinking leaves one staggering and in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: REEL AIL said aloud matches the two-word answer. In Britain this is traditional cask-conditioned beer, championed by a long-running campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional cask beer brewed and served the old way is booze in the old style.

clue.text: Top arguing in court, rejecting pressure

indicators.note: rejecting means the letter for pressure is thrown out of the word

parts.note: a barrister pleading is arguing a case in court
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: The best lawyer in court turns down being pressured.
explanation.definitionFit: Top and foremost are synonyms when describing who comes first in a field.

clue.text: Italian singers in operas composed with no end of style

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters are rearranged
with no tells us a letter is dropped from the word operas
end of means the last letter of the word style

explanation.surface: Singers appear in operas written without any sense of style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no end of style' removes E from OPERAS, leaving OPRAS; 'composed' shuffles IN plus OPRAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian plural form for high female voices denotes a group of singers of that range.

clue.text: Distortion in soft sweet

definitions.meaning: a fudging of the facts, a misleading compromise
a soft crumbly confection made from sugar, butter and milk

explanation.surface: Something twisted hidden inside a soft confection.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both a dodge that bends the truth and a soft sugary confection.

clue.text: A crew lent out for community service

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A team has been loaned out to do work for the community.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is a local office giving free legal advice to the public.
explanation.definitionFit: A local free legal-advice office is a service run for the community.

clue.text: Eccentric owns teeth sharpener

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An oddball has a gadget for sharpening teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone for honing blades is a sharpener.

clue.text: Make stronger use of religious education?

parts.note: RE is the British school abbreviation for religious education
a law that is in use is in force

explanation.surface: A question about the practical use of teaching religion at school.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'use of RE' as RE being in force.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolster or strengthen something, as with steel bars in concrete, is to make it stronger.

clue.text: Young offender to stray — or get better?

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
to rove is to wander or stray

explanation.surface: Will a delinquent go astray or reform?
explanation.definitionFit: To get better is to make progress, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Site of professional shooting?

parts.note: sounds like a hitman's or rifle range, but means where camera filming takes place

explanation.surface: Where a professional killer does his work.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting is filming, so the professional site is a studio stage for a movie.

clue.text: Gentleman confronting two bridge players — one sounds the alarm

parts.note: Sir is the title or form of address for a gentleman
East and North are two of the four players at a bridge table, abbreviated E and N

explanation.surface: A man faces two card players while someone raises an alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A warning hooter on a police car or factory is a device that sounds the alarm.

clue.text: Asian language retained by extremists in struggling party

indicators.note: retained by means held inside the outer letters
the extremists in a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: Hindi is a language of India

explanation.surface: Speakers of an Asian language held by fanatics in a fraught party.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively, noisy party is an informal synonym.

clue.text: Olympic city with diplomatic approach that's read as a severe warning

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Olympics
tact is a diplomatic approach

explanation.surface: An Olympic city reads out a severe warning, tactfully.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was a British law read aloud to disperse crowds; to read it is to scold severely.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase about reading it means to deliver a strong reprimand or stern warning.

clue.text: Drunk needs bit of advice, getting escorted after parking

indicators.note: after places the word for escorted behind the parking letter

parts.note: a tip is a helpful bit of advice
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
led means escorted or guided

explanation.surface: A drunk needs a tip and is escorted away after parking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like a noun but is the past tense of the verb drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To have tippled is to have drunk alcohol, especially habitually; both are past tenses.

clue.text: Object shown in streetside murals

indicators.note: shown in means the answer is displayed inside these words

explanation.surface: A thing displayed in street murals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To object is to raise a protest, a synonym.

clue.text: Mistake regarding small footwear

parts.note: a slip is a small mistake
on means regarding or about
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: An error concerning little shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoes with no laces that are pushed on are a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Work extremely large amount to see marsupial

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: Put in a lot of effort to spot a pouched animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This American pouched mammal is a marsupial, like the kangaroo.

clue.text: Curious dance card

parts.note: odd means curious or strange
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A strange dance card, of the kind used to book partners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' is not a dance card but an old word for an eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is a dated term for a comical, eccentric character, much like an eccentric.

clue.text: Pugilist with sweat covering face — 'Hang on!' we hear

indicators.note: covering its face hides the opening letter of the word for sweat

parts.note: to swelter is to sweat in the heat

indicators.note: we hear says the word for hang on is heard, not written

parts.note: wait means hang on

explanation.surface: A sweaty boxer covers his face and calls for a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer in the class between lightweight and middleweight is a pugilist.
